_metadata.purpose: Names that refer to the SAME PRODUCT but do not collide by spelling. Resolved at load by src/technology-identity.js: the alias's evidence is merged into the canonical entry and the alias name disappears.
_metadata.why_explicit: Case/spacing/punctuation variants (AccessiBe vs accessiBe) are a spelling accident and are collapsed automatically. Vendor renames and product-name changes are NOT derivable from the strings and need human knowledge, so they are recorded here where they can be reviewed rather than guessed.
_metadata.evidence: Each entry below was confirmed by DETECTION-SET overlap over 645 scannable institutions, not by name similarity. See scripts/category-audit.js (CO_OCCURRENCE_DUPLICATE) and docs/category-audit.json.
_metadata.caution: Merging unions the evidence and keeps the canonical's categories. Do NOT add an entry unless the two names are genuinely the same product — high co-occurrence alone is not enough. `Salesforce` and `TargetX` overlap at Jaccard 0.57 because TargetX is BUILT ON Salesforce; they are different products and must stay separate.

reasons.Salesforce Education Cloud: One product, one name (2026-11-16 detection review, finding 4). Nothing on a Salesforce org host distinguishes Education Cloud from Sales Cloud, EDA, TargetX or EnrollmentRx, so the curated entry that carried this name was the generic Salesforce-org signal under an edition name it could not support; it was renamed to `Salesforce` (higher-ed-crm.json), and the second `Salesforce` entry, which fired on the same orgs through an unbounded `(?<!work)force\.com` and duplicated every one of its 16 live rows, was folded into it. This alias keeps any definition still carrying the old name (a restored file, an older artifact being replayed) from coming back as a separate technology.
reasons.Omni CMS: Modern Campus renamed the product: OU Campus → OmniUpdate/OmniCMS → Omni CMS → Modern Campus CMS. Confirmed by detection-set overlap J=0.957 over 67/70 institutions. ⚠️ The base `Omni CMS` entry holds the dom rule a[href*='a.cms.omniupdate.com/11/'] — the ONLY evidence path that made Omni CMS detectable at all before UNI-224, where it was verified 29/29. The merge unions evidence precisely so that rule survives the rename.
reasons.OmniCMS: Same product, older vendor spelling. Also carried its category as the STRING "CMS", which mapCategory lowercased to "cms" and the case-sensitive signal check then dropped — so this entry was silently not counted as a CMS at all.
reasons.Slate: Technolutions Slate, the higher-ed admissions CRM. Detection sets are IDENTICAL (Jaccard 1.00, 111/111 institutions) with `Slate (Technolutions)`. The higher-ed-infra.json entry was tagged cats [52,53] = Chatbot + SIS; its own _validation note already said 'cats [52,53]=Chatbot/SIS is mis-categorized; Slate is an admissions CRM — follow-up'. This is that follow-up. Canonical is the higher-ed-crm.json entry (CRM, id 303); the infra entry's richer evidence (mx.technolutions.net, window.ping_, the Technolutions js global, meta application-name, the x-slate-instance header) is merged in rather than lost.
reasons.TYPO3 CMS: Same product as `TYPO3`; both fired on the same typo3conf/typo3temp assets and the cms_same_product policy only stopped them cancelling each other. (2026-11-16 detection review, finding 7: one signal, two ledger rows.) The canonical is the name the other ledger sources (BuiltWith, WhatCMS) already use, so a deTECHtor row corroborates theirs. On the shared `meta.generator` key the canonical's `TYPO3` wins, which already matches every value the alias's narrower rule did.
reasons.Kentico CMS: Same product as `Kentico` (Kentico Xperience); the alias carried the /CMSPages/GetResource.ashx and kentico.resource asset rules, merged in. (2026-11-16 detection review, finding 7: one signal, two ledger rows.) The canonical is the name the other ledger sources (BuiltWith, WhatCMS) already use, so a deTECHtor row corroborates theirs. On the shared `meta.generator` key the canonical's `Kentico` wins and matches every value the alias's rule did.
reasons.Crisp Live Chat: Same widget (client.crisp.chat) under the WebAppAnalyzer name; identical rules to curated `Crisp`. (2026-11-16 detection review, finding 7: one signal, two ledger rows.) The canonical is the name the other ledger sources (BuiltWith, WhatCMS) already use, so a deTECHtor row corroborates theirs.
reasons.Zendesk Chat: Zopim is Zendesk Chat's legacy embed (v2.zopim.com); the base `Zendesk Chat` entry fired on exactly that host, so both rows came from one tag. Canonical `Zopim`: BuiltWith holds 256 Zopim rows and 0 Zendesk Chat rows in the ledger. (2026-11-16 detection review, finding 7: one signal, two ledger rows.) The canonical is the name the other ledger sources (BuiltWith, WhatCMS) already use, so a deTECHtor row corroborates theirs.
reasons.Genesys Chat: BoldChat was sold by LogMeIn to Genesys; the base `Genesys Chat` entry fired on the same boldchat.com host as `Bold Chat`. Canonical `Bold Chat`: BuiltWith holds 56 Bold Chat rows and 0 Genesys Chat rows. (2026-11-16 detection review, finding 7: one signal, two ledger rows.) The canonical is the name the other ledger sources (BuiltWith, WhatCMS) already use, so a deTECHtor row corroborates theirs.
reasons.BDOW: BDOW is Sumo's later brand; the two base entries carry identical rules (sumo.com / sumome.com, the sumo globals). Canonical `Sumo`: BuiltWith holds 23 Sumo rows and 0 BDOW rows. (2026-11-16 detection review, finding 7: one signal, two ledger rows.) The canonical is the name the other ledger sources (BuiltWith, WhatCMS) already use, so a deTECHtor row corroborates theirs.
